title: Mutating commands return three different data shapes in the JSON envelope
description:
Mutating commands disagree on the shape of `data` in the `{schemaVersion, kind, data, principal}` envelope, so a caller cannot read a written record the same way across the group. Reported by the opum-fleet session via the orchestrator after it cost one session a misread close (a script matching `^status:` on `--plain` matched `task edit` and silently missed `task complete`), and reproduced here against source at a9fbc78.

Three shapes exist today:

- bare record: `task create`, `task edit` -> `data` is the task itself (`data.id`, `data.status`).
- raw mutation result: `task start` / `pause` / `complete` / `archive` / `demote`, `draft create` / `promote` -> `data` is `{kind, task|draft, revision}`, so the record is one level down and the internal `revision` hash leaks.
- planning pair: `milestone create`, `decision create` -> `data` is `{record, result}`.

The second shape also puts a second `kind` inside `data` whose value is `"success"`, shadowing the envelope's own semantic `kind` for anything that reads `.kind` off the wrong level.

Cause (not speculation -- both call sites read): `src/cli/commands/task/index.ts` defines `taskFromMutation` and applies it on the `create` and `edit` branches, unwrapping `{kind, task, revision}` to the task. The lifecycle branches in `src/cli/main.ts` (`complete`/`archive`/`pause`/`start` around line 1884, `demote` around line 1913) pass the service result straight through as `data` with no equivalent unwrap. `src/cli/render.ts` is generic and faithfully renders whatever shape it is handed, so `--plain` inherits the same split -- this is a payload-construction inconsistency, not a rendering one.

Reproduction (source at a9fbc78, scratch workspace):

    quest task edit T-1 --description x --actor a --actor-kind human --plain | grep -c '^status:'   # 1
    quest task start T-1 ... ; quest task complete T-1 ... --plain | grep -c '^status:'             # 0

    task edit     --json -> kind=task.updated   data keys: id,aliases,title,status,...
    task complete --json -> kind=task.completed data keys: kind,task,revision

Deciding what to settle on is the point of the task, not just applying the unwrap: converging the lifecycle group on the bare record is the shape `create`/`edit` already document and the one callers expect, but it is a breaking change for any consumer reading `.data.task`, so it needs a version call. QCLI-103 settled the adjacent question for planning records (they return a record at all) and is Done; it did not unify shapes across groups.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every mutating command in the task lifecycle and draft groups returns the written record directly in data, the shape task create/edit already used
task complete/archive/pause/start/demote no longer emit a second kind field inside data, and no longer leak the internal revision hash unless it is a declared part of the contract
A test asserts the agreed shape across at least one command from each of the task lifecycle, task create/edit and draft groups, so the split cannot silently return
Any breaking change to the payload shape is recorded with its version decision before it ships
Fleet consumers of the old shape are enumerated before the change lands, and the one that breaks is reported to the repository that owns it

plan: 1. Enumerate fleet consumers of the lifecycle/draft payload and record what each needs (orchestrator condition 1) -- done before any code change.
2. Unwrap the lifecycle branches in src/cli/main.ts (complete/archive/pause/start/demote) and the draft branches to emit the bare record, matching taskFromMutation on create/edit.

3. Drop the internal revision hash and the nested kind: success from those envelopes. Leave task edit-batch alone: its data.revision is a declared, tested part of the batch contract and the opum-cli-e2e scale harness consumes it.
4. Leave milestone/decision {record, result} as-is: the ruling scopes this to the lifecycle and draft groups. File the planning-group divergence separately if it still matters.
5. Add a test asserting the bare-record shape across task create/edit, a lifecycle command, and draft create/promote so the split cannot silently return.
6. Update the manifest/docs for the changed kinds, run bun run check, land on dev. No release: minor bump riding the next stacked CLI release per OPAG-65.
implementationNotes:
Consumer enumeration (orchestrator condition 1), done before any code change. Grepped opum-cli-e2e, lore-cli, opum-doc, opum-agent, opum-fleet, opum-marketplace, quest-web, lore-web, opum-web, opum-bridge, opum-harness, opum-session and ~/.claude plugins for reads of .data.task/.draft/.record/.revision and for callers of the lifecycle and draft commands.

BREAKS (1, in a repo I do not own): opum-cli-e2e suites/40-cross-product.mjs:166 reads parseEnvelope(pause.stdout).value?.data?.task?.status with no fallback, and line 183 asserts it equals the configured paused status. After the unwrap that read yields undefined and the check fails. opum-cli-e2e owns the fix -- add the ?? data?.status fallback its other reads already use. Must be told before this lands in a qualified pair.

SURVIVES, already defensive: opum-cli-e2e suites/21-quest-records.mjs:43,60,78,388,425 and 40-cross-product.mjs:704 all read data?.id ?? data?.task?.id; suites/21-quest-records.mjs:254,294 read data?.id ?? data?.draft?.id. These were written to tolerate both shapes and keep working after the change -- the .task fallback simply goes dead.

SURVIVES, primary path unaffected: opum-cli-e2e suites/45-parity-backlog.mjs:212 reads status from a following task view and only falls back to questData(questComplete)?.task?.status. The fallback dies, the assertion does not.

UNAFFECTED: lore-cli src/adapters/quest.ts REQUIRED_COMMANDS (lines 106-119) covers manifest, version, init, the migration group, task status-flow/list/view/search/create/edit -- no lifecycle or draft command, so the adapter never sees these payloads. opum-workflow hooks (flush-state.sh, _lib.sh, session-start.sh in the opum-fleet plugin cache) use task list --json, task view --plain and task edit --add-note only. opum-doc, opum-agent and opum-fleet hits are prose or historical evidence/baseline artifacts, not live consumers.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: task edit-batch keeps data.revision. It is asserted in test/qcli122-third-pass.test.ts:263-264 and consumed by opum-cli-e2e bin/opum-e2e-scale.mjs:312 for chunked batch progress, so it is a declared part of the batch contract rather than a leak. Only the lifecycle and draft envelopes drop it. milestone/decision {record, result} also stays: the ruling scopes this to the lifecycle and draft groups, and opum-cli-e2e suites/45-parity-backlog.mjs:293,298,448 read .record?.id today.

Version call (orchestrator condition 2), recorded before the change lands. This is a breaking payload change to the lifecycle and draft envelopes and takes a MINOR bump from 0.6.0 to 0.7.0 under 0.x semantics. It lands on dev behind the repo's own checks and is NOT released on its own: it rides the next stacked CLI release in lockstep with lore, per OPAG-65's standing rule. No npm publish, no tag, no version field bump in this change -- the release that carries it sets the number. opum-cli-e2e must land its 40-cross-product.mjs fallback fix before that pair is qualified, or the pair run fails on a defect this task created.

Implemented on branch fix/QCLI-264-mutation-payload-shape, PR #1 into dev (commit b6ed063).

Change: a shared recordFromMutation in src/cli/commands/task/index.ts, applied to the five lifecycle branches and the three draft branches in src/cli/main.ts. taskFromMutation stays as the create/edit path it always was. src/cli/render.ts is untouched -- --plain inherits the corrected shape because it renders whatever payload it is handed, which is also why the original --plain symptom was never a rendering defect.

Second defect fixed as a consequence, found while reading the code rather than reported: a write conflict on those routes used to return a SUCCESS envelope at exit 0 with kind: 'conflict' nested in data, because the raw mutation result was passed through without inspecting its kind. recordFromMutation throws tracker_write_conflict on any non-success, which main.ts already maps to the documented conflict failure at exit 5. task create/edit never had this -- taskFromMutation already classified it.

Tests updated rather than deleted: test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts (the declared-envelopes route test and the createdAt/updatedAt stamping test both asserted data.task/data.draft), test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts (the QCLI-229 pause/start/demote assertions). New test/qcli264-mutation-payload-shape.test.ts pins the bare shape across create/edit, all five lifecycle commands and the draft group, asserts the absence of the task/draft/revision/kind wrapper keys, reproduces the original ^status: symptom over --plain in both directions, and pins edit-batch's revision as the deliberate exception so a later sweep does not strip it.

Verification: bun run check green -- 446 pass, 0 fail across 50 files, typecheck, lint, format and layer checks clean. The one pre-existing lint warning (unused 'error' binding in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts:374) is untouched and unrelated.

Out of scope, filed as QCLI-265 rather than silently widened: milestone/decision create keep {record, result}, and draft view keeps the located {draft, location} read shape while task view is bare.

Delivery defects to record rather than repeat, both mine:

1. The first tracker commit (5852092, 'record the mutating-command payload shape split') went straight to dev with no branch and no PR. The opum-sdlc skill is explicit that a .quest-only change takes the same path as any other -- branch, PR, squash -- because a direct commit to dev is invisible to review and to delete_branch_on_merge hygiene. The code change itself went through PR #1 correctly.

2. I ran 'gh pr merge 1 --squash --delete-branch' with tracker edits uncommitted in the working tree. The merge SUCCEEDED server-side; only the local branch-switch step aborted, printing 'Please commit your changes or stash them' -- which reads exactly like the whole command failed. I then committed to a branch that had already been squash-merged and deleted, stranding the tracker records until I cherry-picked them onto chore/QCLI-264-tracker-records (PR #2). Lesson: gh pr merge's failure output does not distinguish 'the merge did not happen' from 'the merge happened and cleanup did not'. Check 'gh pr view --json state' before reacting to it, and commit or stash first.
finalSummary:
Every mutating command now carries the written record directly in the envelope's data, the shape task create/edit already used. task complete/archive/pause/start/demote and draft create/promote/archive previously nested it under data.task/data.draft alongside the repository revision hash and a second kind: 'success' that shadowed the envelope's own semantic kind, so a caller that could read one group could not read the other.

Cause was a missing unwrap, not a design: src/cli/commands/task/index.ts had taskFromMutation on the create and edit branches and the lifecycle branches in src/cli/main.ts had no equivalent. All of them now go through a shared recordFromMutation. render.ts is untouched -- --plain inherited the corrected shape by itself, confirming the reported --plain symptom was never a rendering defect.

A second defect was fixed as a consequence, found by reading the code rather than reported: a write conflict on those routes used to return a SUCCESS envelope at exit 0 carrying kind: 'conflict' inside data. It is now the documented conflict failure at exit 5.

Verified, not assumed: bun run check green (446 pass, 0 fail across 50 files); PR #1 green on all ten platform and source-gate checks and squash-merged to dev as d91c648. New test/qcli264-mutation-payload-shape.test.ts pins the bare shape across create/edit, all five lifecycle commands and the draft group, asserts the wrapper keys are absent, reproduces the original ^status: symptom over --plain in both directions, and pins edit-batch's revision as the deliberate exception. Three existing tests that asserted the old nesting were updated rather than deleted.

Consumers were enumerated across twelve fleet repos and the installed plugin cache before any code changed. One hard break (opum-cli-e2e suites/40-cross-product.mjs:166), reported to that repo, which has landed a both-shapes-tolerant fix as its PR #80 with no dependency on this release. That session independently re-derived the sweep and found one call site my grep missed (45-parity-backlog.mjs:250, safe -- its fallback is written in the reverse order); the sweep is closed with that correction, and the search defect is recorded, since matching the idiom rather than the field name is what hid it.

Not released: minor bump under 0.x, riding the next stacked CLI release in lockstep with lore per OPAG-65. Out of scope by ruling and filed as QCLI-265: milestone/decision keep {record, result}, and draft view keeps the located {draft, location} read shape against a bare task view.



Post-close correction (2026-09-11): the headline wording of this change claimed a universal it does not make. The changelog entry, the recordFromMutation comment and the contract test's own name all said 'every mutating command carries the record directly in data'. task edit-batch does not and deliberately does not -- it is a batch report whose records stay at data.items[].task with its declared data.revision. The changelog qualified it two paragraphs down, but the first sentence is the one that gets quoted, and it was: opum-fleet shipped the universal into opum-workflow's quest-writes.md on the strength of my phrasing plus their own two measurements, then caught it by measuring edit-batch and corrected it (OFLE-9). Narrowed to 'every single-record mutating command' in all three places, with the qualifier leading rather than trailing and edit-batch named as a reason rather than an oversight. The rule worth keeping: when a claim has an exception, the exception belongs in the same sentence -- a qualifier two paragraphs later does not travel with the quote.



Second post-close correction (2026-09-11): the justification recorded for keeping task edit-batch's data.revision was wrong in strength, though the decision it supported still stands. I wrote that 'chunked callers page on it' and that opum-cli-e2e's scale harness depends on it. Measured at bin/opum-e2e-scale.mjs:312 by that repo's own session and re-read here: the only fleet read of the field is one interpolation in a progress log line, and paging runs off that harness's own chunk bookkeeping on the very next line (persistState) which never consults it. Strip the field and that log prints 'revision undefined'; nothing else moves. The field is still kept, on the reasoning that actually holds: it is the workspace revision the batch committed at, which is what a caller needs for the bounded retry this CLI explicitly does not do for them, and test/qcli122-third-pass.test.ts has pinned it since QCLI-122. Corrected in the changelog and in the test comment, which now says why the pin exists AND names what it is not. Rule worth keeping alongside the first: a dependency reported at the wrong strength is as misleading as one reported at the wrong location -- 'a sibling depends on this' is exactly the kind of reason that keeps a field alive for years after the dependency is gone, so a pin should record the dependency's strength, not just its existence.
